page: Microsoft Azure B4ls_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the low-memory tier of the Bsv2 series. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 4 vCPUs backed by 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB total, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and includes no dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-thread compute capabilities counterbalanced by modest multi-core scaling. The Intel Xeon 8370C architecture delivers average single-core throughput, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1635.0 and gzip compression at 28.71 GB/sec. However, multi-core tasks show typical burstable constraints, scoring in the lower quartiles with 3495.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 3872.77 on stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory throughput is limited, marked by a PassMark memory score of 1126.86 and an uncached read bandwidth of 30.2 GB/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and burstable credit model provide an economical operational baseline for systems with intermittent CPU utilization. Workloads requiring continuous full-core execution or large memory footprints will experience throughput limitations. The configuration is best aligned with low-traffic web services, background queuing workers, microservices, and development environments that do not require local ephemeral storage.
description: Microsoft Azure B4ls_v2 is an entry-level burstable instance featuring 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Configured with 8.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a reduced memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, without local temporary storage or onboard GPU acceleration. Architectural benchmarks highlight balanced single-threaded performance alongside constrained multi-core throughput and moderate memory bandwidth. This hardware setup suits variable, non-continuous workloads such as development or testing nodes, lightweight application servers, low-concurrency web tiers, and auxiliary CI/CD tasks that accommodate burstable CPU scheduling.
